basic_info.headline: Embedded Software Engineer
basic_info.about: I am a software engineer with over 18 years of industry experience, specializing in the development of software for embedded devices. My education and experience are in the field of Electrical Engineering, with a focus on computer and software engineering in particular. I am based in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, and I have spent over a decade and a half working full-time in the Metro Detroit area. I am fully committed to excellence, integrity, and professionalism in everything that I do.

experience.title: Embedded Software Engineer
experience.description: I worked on a team of embedded software engineers who are developing production-quality embedded software for an Infotainment ECU for upcoming GM vehicle programs. The team develops embedded software in the C language for one particular microcontroller in the ECU which enables it to interface with other ECUs in a vehicle. My primary focus on this team has been to develop the diagnostics functionality of the Infotainment system, which enables the identification of vehicle problems both in the assembly plant and in the service garage. I also regularly provide technical support to the assembly plants as our software enters full production.

experience.title: Embedded Software Engineer DevQA
experience.description: In this role, I worked on a team of software engineers who are developing embedded software for an Infotainment ECU. This is the same team as my current role. I supported this team by engaging in Development Quality Assurance (DevQA) activities, and by working closely with the developers to ensure that the software is properly and effectively tested prior to release.

experience.title: Software Tools Engineer
experience.description:
In my role as a Software Tools Engineer, I was responsible for the development of tools which are primarily used for the validation of pre-production telematics (OnStar) and Infotainment hardware.  These tools are used by local and international development and validation teams.  

Major accomplishments:

1. GM is expanding the OnStar brand into new global markets.  This rapid expansion meant that some of OnStar's existing validation tools were becoming outdated or were unsuitable for use by engineers in locations outside of the U.S.  In order to accommodate this expansion, some new tools were needed which could be used by international teams.  One of those was an application which could simulate the functionality of the OnStar Call Center.  I worked with a small team of engineers to develop and deploy the new Call Center simulator, which is a client/server application written in C# and ASP.NET.  The project took about a year and a half to complete.  The new application has shown itself to be more stable, reliable and scalable than our legacy Call Center simulator, and it is currently being used by approximately 500 engineers in various regions of the world.

2. I developed a suite of administrative and status monitoring applications to complement the new Call Center simulator application.  Using the administrative applications, select users can make changes to the server databases remotely.  I also successfully automated several important business processes which were previously handled manually.  The status monitoring applications provide an at-a-glance view of the system's status and volume of usage.

3. Shortly after joining the Software Tools Team in 2011, I worked alongside several other engineers to upgrade an existing Call Center simulator to support the validation of the OnStar 4G LTE program.  Our department director gave us an Engineering Excellence award for completing this project in a timely manner.

education.degree: Master of Applied Science (M.A.Sc.), Electrical Engineering
education.description:
During the course of my graduate studies, my thesis research focused on the area of embedded soft processor design targeting Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs).  Many soft processors have numerous configurable parameters, each of which may have several possible values.  A large number of parameters and values from which to choose yields a large design space, which is essentially the set of all possible configurations.  Having a large design space and multiple objectives to optimize means that selecting a good configuration for a given application can be a challenge.

For my thesis, I conducted an investigation of the feasibility of using a genetic algorithm to explore the design space of embedded CPU cores.  During this research, I developed a Computer Aided Design tool in C++ called SC Build, which implemented a genetic algorithm called the Simple Evolutionary Algorithm of Multi-Objective Optimization (SEAMO) which I used to explore the design space of CPUs targeting Altera FPGAs.

education.degree: Bachelor of Applied Science (B.A.Sc.), Electrical Engineering
education.description: My undergraduate studies focused on the area of Computer Engineering.  For my fourth year project, I worked on a small team to a develop a Pulse-Width Modulation (PWM) controller for a cooling fan from a BMW SUV.  For this project, we modified a Tetris cartridge for the old Nintendo Gameboy system.  We created custom software in C and Assembly and loaded it onto an EEPROM we had soldered to the cartridge.  With this prototype, we were able to successfully spin the fan at different speeds using the Gameboy's control pad.
